feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Within the Bitcoin protocol, there are six canonical SIGHASH types under legacy and BIP143 rules: 1, 2, 3, 0x81, 0x82, and 0x83. Despite this, all 256 possible SIGHASH type values are recognized as distinct and valid at the consensus level. This flexibility allows adversarial miners to exploit non-standard SIGHASH types, effectively undermining any effort to cache signature hash (sighash) values. As a result, it becomes necessary to recompute the transaction digest for each OP_CHECKSIG operation, regardless of whether OP_CODESEPARATOR is used.
To mitigate these issues, a potential solution would involve rejecting OP_CODESEPARATOR, FindAndDelete(), and non-standard SIGHASH types through a soft fork. However, this approach proves ineffective with the next-generation SIGHASH scheme, which introduces numerous standard sighash types. Furthermore, in Segregated Witness (SegWit), the previous O(n²) hashing inefficiency has been resolved, rendering sighash caching both unnecessary and inefficient.
Sighash caching does not offer compelling benefits in the new SIGHASH framework and does not justify the removal of OP_CODESEPARATOR, especially considering that some users derive value from its functionality. Nevertheless, deprecating OP_CODESEPARATOR in legacy scripts remains advisable. While general opinion tends to be against OP_CODESEPARATOR, a more nuanced, case-by-case evaluation is warranted to ensure that decisions do not unnecessarily limit useful features.
